horizontal.escena:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE independent full-bleed narrative or symbolic PHYSICAL PAPER-CUT artwork, never a three-panel collage. All reference images are OUR OWN AI-generated visual-bible sheets. Use their identities, shapes and material language, not their multiple-view layouts, cropped auxiliary portraits or white specimen insets. Very expressive handcrafted thick matte dyed cardstock: clear pale cut cross-sections, lifted and curled edges, separated shadows between actual layers, deliberate hand-cut curves, folded leaf midribs, cut and folded feather vanes, visibly woven paper fibres, water as overlapping blue sheets and ripples. Heads and faces use few QUIET paper planes with natural proportions; no polygon-faceted CGI cheekbones, shiny skin, plastic dolls or digital-paint substitutes. Whole principal bodies, feet, wings, snouts, tails and ornament tips remain inside frame. The environmental world continues outside all four edges; no visible plinth, frame, diorama perimeter, tabletop, collage, model-sheet layout or printed text. Material depth comes between world layers. Colors differentiate each actor and each narrative rather than cloning the same hunter. Preserve proper reference clothes: bark/fibre covers and sparse seeds, feathers and small quill ornaments where present, no modern shirts, trousers, ponchos or synthetic beads. When a character has a pale nasal quill in the reference, make its near tip plainly visible at the nostril base against skin. No real-person likeness, private-photo reuse, medical or ritual instructions. This is original editorial art of the frozen adaptation, not a certified traditional motif.

MYTH: Kugï y Nokuerai: patos y muchachas perdidas. FORMAT: horizontal 16:9, preferably 1536 x 864. FUNCTION: ENTRADA: expansive environmental situation opening the myth; figures small within the world, not a giant portrait.
Reference 1: A13 — Kugï y Nokuerai · patos viajeros. 
Reference 2: A09-53 — Jikueraño · mariposas azules. 
Reference 3: H01-53 — Joyareño y Buynaiyarai · familia de Rikoño. Joyareño wide-cheek face, shoulder black hair, plain cream below-knee garment with a large RED/charcoal FRONT zigzag, bare head, pale quill nasal ornament, brown/red seed strand. Father: LOW dark/green feather crown, four sparse cream curved pendants, narrow bark cover with ochre cord, no nasal pin. Mother: short grey-black chin hair, plain cream longer garment with ochre neck edge, TWO tiny red feather EAR tufts, a small pale nose quill, sparse black/cream seed strand. Infant is a separate H14, never a school-age child.
Reference 4: L03 — Río · ribera baja y paso. 

PRIMARY SCENE / OPERATION:
Wide sapphire river through low Amazonian banks at dawn. A small orderly group of exactly FOUR whole river ducks like A13 swims upstream in a clear continuous line. On the near bank TWO fully clothed young adult women, proposed using the female grammar of H01-53 without claiming those support names as the sisters, follow several whole small blue butterflies A09-53. One editorial impossible route: the butterflies' folded blue ribbon shadow loops back to the SAME stepping place on the bank, while duck wakes remain directed upstream. No boats, bird-human hybrids, nudity, giant butterflies or invented mapped rivers. Entire two women and ducks fit, expansive territory and opposing routes dominate.

VISIBLE CHECK: Patos avanzan con dirección; dos jóvenes siguen un recorrido que vuelve al mismo paso.

vertical.escena:
Use case: image editing. Edit OUR OWN AI-GENERATED paper-cut original, reference image 1. Make one independent full-bleed artwork in vertical 9:16, preferably 864 x 1536.

CORRECTION:
REMOVE the physical green-blue parrot entirely. In its place create a single PARROT-SHAPED SHADOW on the earthen floor, visibly CONNECTED to the whole woman Rikoño shadow at her feet and crossing into the dark maloca doorway. The ONLY physical principal figure is the unchanged whole Rikoño, with her complete feet, blue feather tuft, small nasal quill, cheek spirals, ochre-cream-black fibre dress and cream pendant necklace. Preserve the doorway, light and handmade paper relief. This shadow makes transformation visible; do not add a physical bird, duplicate woman or extra props.

Preserve expressive physical matte cardstock, actual separated layer shadows, pale cut cross-sections, hand-cut curves, folded feather vanes and leaf midribs. Quiet natural paper-plane faces, no CGI, plastic or digital painting. The environment continues beyond all four borders; no frame, plinth or specimen-sheet layout. No printed text. Every principal whole body, head, hand, foot, wing and ornament tip must remain inside the canvas. Retain the original color relationships and traditional fibre covers. These are original editorial illustrations, not certified traditional symbols. No private photo, real-person likeness or ritual instructions.

MYTH: Kugï y Nokuerai: patos y muchachas perdidas. FORMAT: square 1:1, 1024 x 1024. FUNCTION: HUELLA: ONE primary motif plus ONE impossible symbolic operation, readable at thumbnail; not a third literal scene, parade of props or empty landscape.
Reference 1: V18 — Rikoño: lora. 
Reference 2: L01 — Maloca — exterior e interior. 

PRIMARY SCENE / OPERATION:
ONE whole natural PARROT FEATHER, vivid emerald with a small cobalt edge, lies just OUTSIDE a raised ochre cut-paper DOORWAY-shaped gap. The feather's ONE shadow passes cleanly through that gap, but the physical feather remains outside; the gap is a negative-space portal in a continuous earth/forest paper layer, not literal furniture or a miniature house. Original editorial metaphor for Rikoño's return that cannot restore the old belonging. No people, actual parrot body, words, musical notation, knife or other props. Feather plus unreachable threshold is one relational symbol, complete and clear at thumbnail size.

VISIBLE CHECK: Pluma exterior cuya sombra atraviesa un umbral al que ella no entra.
